criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-context`. A new test builds the reader brief and asserts it contains a 'Rules that judge criteria' section that states D43's evidence rule (including that a recorded passing Athena check on the same tree counts), that docs/decisions.md and records/ entries are append-only (new decision, not an in-place edit), and that the default-required CHANGELOG.md deliverable cannot be forbidden. The test fails on the base commit and passes with the change.
criteria.evidence: I ran it and it passed (1 passed). The test builds `reader_brief(&reader_inputs(&reading()))`, extracts the `# Rules that judge criteria` section, and asserts the following lines: D43 ('must cite commands that ran (D43)', 'recorded Athena check'), D63, D115 ('passing check that Athena recorded on the same final tree', 'a failed record, or a record made on another tree, does not count'), append-only ('docs/decisions.md is append-only', 'records are append-only', 'new appended decision with a Provenance bullet') and Changelog ('default-written deliverable', 'must not forbid changing it'). Athena's fails-without-1 record shows the same command exiting 101 when the fix is reverted. It failed to compile because the constants it uses did not exist yet, and without the section the heading lookup would fail as well.

criteria.criterion: A second new test in crates/athena-context shows the section's rule text matches the constants or wording used by the enforcing code, so it fails if the enforcing rule changes and the brief does not. It covers the cause class, not one job.
criteria.evidence: I ran both and both passed. The first test reads verify.rs, checks.rs, mirrors.rs, admission.rs and athena-gate/src/lib.rs with include_str!. It slices VERDICT_RULES and asserts that VERDICT_RULE_LINES equals the parsed (id, source) rows, so a new or reworded row fails it. It also checks the DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES literals, and checks the three enforcing phrases against production code only (the text before #[cfg(test)]). I confirmed the phrases sit at the cited places: mirrors.rs:265, admission.rs:999, athena-gate lib.rs:101 and checks.rs:574-577. The second test shows the helpers report a made-up row, a reworded source and an extra literal as missing. The rules covered (verdict rules, append-only logs, default-written files) span the whole class, not one job.

findings.summary: The pin tests parse other crates' source text, so they depend on how that text is laid out.
findings.evidence: If VERDICT_RULES is reformatted (for example `id:` and `source:` on one line) or a literal gains an escaped quote, the parse breaks. The failure messages name the file to update, and D174's Tradeoff states the cost. The crate dependency direction rules out a cleaner shared const, so this is acceptable.

findings.summary: The 'meaning' text of each verdict line is a paraphrase that no test pins.
findings.evidence: Only `source` is compared with verify.rs, so the explanation could drift from the enforced rule unnoticed. Test 1 asserts key phrases of the current meaning, but nothing ties them to the enforcing code.

summary: The change fixes the cause where it starts. The reader brief now has a `# Rules that judge criteria` section, built in code, that gives the reader the facts it lacked: the verdict rules D43, D63 and D115 (a passing check Athena recorded on the same tree counts), that docs/decisions.md and records/ are append-only (add a new decision, never edit one), and that the default-written CHANGELOG.md cannot be forbidden. No refusal rule is added; the declared share is 0% and Athena's replay found 0 of 50 accepted readings newly refused. I ran the three new athena-context tests and the prompt budget test, and all passed. Athena's records show fmt, clippy and the full test suite passing on this tree, and show the new tests failing (exit 101) when the fix is reverted. The pin test ties the section to VERDICT_RULES, DEFAULT_WRITTEN_FILES and the enforcing phrases in production code, and a drift-helper test shows that pin catches added or reworded rows. decisions.md only gains appended lines (D174), no prompt file changed, and every changed file is on the deliverables list. The only findings are two nits: the pin tests parse source text, and each rule's explanation text is not pinned.
